about: Inazio Urruzola is a family estate in Alkiza, a hill village in Gipuzkoa beneath the limestone massif of Mount Hernio, inland from San Sebastián. According to its US sellers, the farmstead began as an apple press, for cider, in 1348, and the same family has worked the land for eleven generations, eventually replacing orchards with vines. Today the estate pairs its winery with a restaurant serving traditional Basque tasting menus, in a building inspired by the Basque sculptor Jorge Oteiza.

The vineyards sit around 1,000 feet above sea level and are farmed sustainably and picked by hand. The 2024 is 90% Hondarrabi Zuri with 10% Petit Corbu, a rare old grape from the Pyrenees that adds a little weight and perfume. A past vintage’s notes describe the method as cool fermentation in stainless steel with a few weeks on the lees, keeping the natural spritz that gives txakoli its lift. At 10.5% alcohol it is light and very refreshing.

Expect citrus zest and green apple, a salty, mineral edge and bright acidity, in the classic style of the coast. The wine has been poured on the tasting menu at Arzak, the three-Michelin-star restaurant in San Sebastián, and it is at its best with shellfish, fish and soft cheeses, served well chilled and drunk young.
facts: Hand harvested; fermented cool in stainless steel
